correctness.rationale: Proposition 10 reduces maximum size to a finite integer optimization. Reversal permits x1<=y1. For fixed x1 through x3, the objective is affine in x5 and then affine in x4 after choosing x5 optimally, so checking the two x4 endpoints is exhaustive. Integer enumeration yields one reduced optimum for each q=7,8,9; Proposition 11 and q>=3 partition uniqueness give the exact code counts. A standalone verifier reproduces the enumeration, and the public reference solver independently matches all three optimum values and profiles.

value.rationale: The three cases extend the exact length-six frontier immediately beyond the published q<=6 table. The q=9 case is structurally informative: after q=7 and q=8 retain the simple one-boundary extremizer, q=9 requires a nontrivial second partition and gains 258 words over the best k=5 Blackburn code. Exact N(q,6) values and full optimal profiles make the transition reusable for testing conjectures and algorithms for maximum non-overlapping codes.
